title: Play with Time
use_cases: Use when building suspense by revealing outcomes before their causes
Implement when managing multiple complex timelines that converge in a finale
Configure when seeking to subvert standard chronological story structures
Use when the mystery of 'how' it happened is more important than 'what' happened
content: When you play with time, you play with the reader’s anticipation. Many books have event A lead to event B, which leads to event C. Showing your reader a hint of event C, then switching to part of A, and then transitioning to the middle of B will keep the reader wanting to know how it all connects. You can reverse or mix up the order of events to slowly reveal the full picture. You can also merge different timelines and even completely different stories—that connect somehow in the end of course. This arrangement subverts reader expectations by breaking from a standard chronological narrative.
